articles.title: Barricade stunt, chips, 9-hour dharna and detentions: All that happened at Rahul Gandhi-led CEC protest
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: High drama unfolded in the heart of Delhi on Tuesday as INDIA bloc MPs marched towards the Election Commission demanding Chief Election
articles.body: NEW DELHI: High drama unfolded in the heart of Delhi on Tuesday as INDIA bloc MPs marched towards the Election Commission demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.The day-long protest ended after Delhi Police detained Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, KC Venugopal, Amrinder Singh Raja Warring, Charanjit Singh Channi, and several other opposition MPs at Akashvani Bhavan, where they staged a sit-in after being denied a meeting with election officials.The protest was part of the INDIA bloc's wider campaign against the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.Opposition parties have accused the poll panel of disenfranchising eligible voters and have demanded Kumar's resignation. They have also sought the scrapping of the ongoing SIR exercise and the restoration of names they allege were wrongly deleted from electoral rolls.Here are the top developments from the opposition protest:Rahul leads the marchRahul Gandhi, along with several opposition leaders, began the march from Parliament towards the Election Commission headquarters, raising slogans of "Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod" and carrying placards and cutouts of Gyanesh Kumar.The protest route saw heavy security deployment, with barricades placed across central Delhi and Rapid Action Force personnel deployed around Transport Bhawan ahead of the march. Police stopped the opposition MPs near the NITI Aayog office.Rahul climbed atop heavy iron barricades near the NITI Aayog office and waved the Tricolour as he attempted to advance towards the EC headquarters.Tensions escalated as Delhi Police detained Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Congress general secretary KC Venugopal and several other INDIA bloc leaders near the NITI Aayog office.Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, Trinamool Congress leaders Abhishek Banerjee, Derek O'Brien and Mahua Moitra, and CPM MP John Brittas were among those put into police buses.Rahul, Priyanka enter Akashvani BhavanThe protest took an unexpected turn when Rahul and Priyanka walked into the nearby Akashvani Bhavan, shifting the protest away from the heavily secured route.As police began detaining INDIA bloc MPs and putting them into buses, Rahul spoke to his sister, who was seated inside one of the buses, before making his way towards the reception entrance of Akashvani Bhavan, catching several opposition MPs, including some from his own party, by surprise.At the entrance near gate number 3, Akashvani Bhavan staff initially tried to prevent Rahul Gandhi from entering, leading to a tense stand-off. He eventually entered the premises accompanied by his security personnel.Around 12.45 pm, Congress general secretary KC Venugopal and Rajya Sabha MP Pawan Khera reached the gate and sought entry. New Delhi deputy commissioner of police Sachin Sharma also arrived and held talks with the leaders, who were subsequently allowed inside.Nine-hour sit inAfter Rahul and other Congress leaders positioned themselves inside Akashvani Bhavan, mats were laid out and the sit-in began.While Rahul remained mostly seated, Priyanka Gandhi held talks with police officials.Refreshments were brought in for the protesters. Packets of potato chips, bhujiya and chocolates, along with water bottles and soft drinks, arrived from a kiosk outside NITI Aayog. Diet Coke was brought from Patel Chowk, while rolls arrived from Khan Chacha.Later, Srinivas was seen clearing used packets from the area where the leaders had gathered. Mosquito repellent was also brought inside in the evening.The crowd outside Akashvani Bhavan grew as Congress workers gathered and raised slogans in support of Rahul Gandhi.Around 2.30 pm, reporters pushed their microphones through the grille as Rahul spoke to them from inside the premises."I don't care what the BJP says. I am standing here to protect democracy," he said."What has been done to the country is treason. Be it PM Modi, Shah, the RSS chief or Gyanesh Kumar, none will be spared," Gandhi alleged.BJP hits backAmid the protest, the BJP held three press conferences and accused Congress and its allies of creating "anarchy" to "relaunch Rahul Gandhi".The BJP also accused Gandhi of being "kaamchor", alleging that he should work on the ground instead of accusing others of being "vote chor".Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan accused the INDIA bloc of "venting its frustration" over electoral defeats by making baseless allegations against constitutional bodies and attempting to malign their image.BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi criticised the opposition for what he called "theatrics on the streets" and questioned the Congress over its demand to provide voting rights without verification to those identified as "absent, shifted, dead and duplicate" voters.Rahul, Priyanka detainedAfter several hours of protest, Delhi Police cleared the site and detained Rahul and Priyanka along with several opposition MPs, including Pawan Khera, KC Venugopal, Amrinder Singh Raja Warring, Derek O'Brien and Mahua Moitra.According to Delhi Police, around 260 individuals, including 10 Parliamentarirans, were detained and taken to various police stations in Delhi, where necessary legal action is being taken in their regard. The detainees were taken to New Police Lines at Kingsway Camp.Congress hit out at the Modi government, saying the action was a sign of a regime that "knows its exit is imminent"."Method of disenfranchising Indians has just become murder of democracy in India," Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said."The leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has been dragged away from a peaceful sit-in protest that had a simple and straightforward demand - a meeting with the Election Commission of India," Ramesh said in a post on X."The Delhi Police that is controlled by the co-conspirator of the murder of democracy in India has arrested the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha and others. This is the sign of a regime that knows its exit is imminent," he added.EC issues clarificationMeanwhile, the Election Commission said no political party had formally sought an appointment for a meeting with it."Earlier today, during the march of certain political parties towards the Election Commission, it was learnt through the media that some Members of Parliament wished to meet the Commission along with their delegation. With regard to today's developments, it is clarified that, till 4.00 PM today, no political party, through its representatives, had sought an appointment for a meeting with the Election Commission," the EC said in a statement.The poll panel said it subsequently learnt through Delhi Police that a delegation of MPs, led by leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, wanted to meet the Commission and submit a memorandum.The EC said its established procedure requires political parties or joint delegations to seek appointments through their authorised representatives. Meetings are then held at a mutually agreed time at the Commission's premises.The poll panel said that after 4 pm, while it was considering the proposed meeting, Delhi Police informed it that the delegation comprised 240 MPs and wanted to meet at the Parliament House Annexe.The Commission termed the request "unusual" and said it could not be accepted because, under ECI protocol, meetings with political parties are held only at the Commission's premises.The INDIA bloc's protest was part of its wider campaign against the Election Commission over the SIR exercise. Opposition parties have accused the poll panel of disenfranchising eligible voters and have demanded Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.The bloc has also sought the scrapping of the current SIR exercise and restoration of names it alleges were wrongly deleted from electoral rolls.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2021, Sheba planted coral onto huge steel letters underwater; the reef campaign lifted in-store sales 10.4% and delivered 308% ROI
articles.summary: Sheba's innovative coral restoration project off Sulawesi, Indonesia, not only revitalized marine life but also contributed to a significant 10.4% increase in store sales and an impressive 308% ROI, merging environmental sustainability with impactful advertising.
articles.body: Mars-owned cat-food brand Sheba turned an underwater coral restoration project off Sulawesi, Indonesia, into a giant advertising campaign in 2021, where thousands of steel structures were placed on the seabed and arranged to spell “HOPE” across a reef that was roughly the length of an Olympic swimming pool, following which, coral was grown across the structures. The project was called Hope Reef, and Sheba launched it as part of a wider coral restoration programme, and combined an environmental project with digital advertising, Google Maps and a YouTube campaign. The campaign later reported a 10.4% increase in physical-store sales and a 308% return on investment.The letters were built from Reef StarsSheba used a restoration system called Reef Stars, steel structures that are designed to stabilise damaged coral rubble and provide a surface where coral fragments can grow. Google's account of the campaign says that the team worked with marine scientists to determine how large the installation needed to be for the word “HOPE” to appear clearly on Google Maps, and the completed reef stretched roughly the length of an Olympic swimming pool.The Reef Star structures were handmade by local residents, and were placed over an area of damaged seabed near the Indonesian island of Sulawesi, where destructive fishing had previously damaged the reef. Sheba's campaign team then built the advertising around the actual restoration work, with Google Maps allowing people to view the reef from above, while underwater imagery showed the coral growing across the installation. The physical advertising structure was also intended to disappear visually as coral growth expanded, and the steel framework remained beneath the reef while living coral covered more of it.Coral cover rose at the siteSheba and its partners reported that coral cover at the site increased substantially after the restoration began. The campaign's corporate reporting later stated that the reef reached about 70% coral coverage, in comparison with less than 2% at the start of the project. Fish abundance also increased by about 300%, according to the campaign's case study.The environmental work was carried out with marine scientists and local partners, while the marketing campaign was used to bring attention to the project. Mars announced Hope Reef in May 2021 as the first site in a programme that aimed to restore more than 185,000 square metres of coral reef around the world by 2029. The company said that the reef was intended to be visible through Google Earth and that advertising revenue from a dedicated YouTube channel would be directed toward additional reef restoration. WPP's 2022 annual report recorded 2.5 billion earned-media impressions and said that the project generated a 308% return on investment. More than one million people explored Hope Reef through Google Maps.The campaign produced a sales increase tooThe commercial numbers were important for Sheba because the project was designed to connect environmental restoration with the brand rather than run as a conventional corporate donation. The campaign case study reported a 10.4% increase in physical-store sales, and also recorded a 308% return on investment, with the environmental project forming the central creative idea behind the campaign. The marketing team also launched a YouTube channel in which advertising revenue from views was directed toward reef restoration, and Google reported that the channel generated hundreds of thousands of hours of viewing during its early months. The campaign later raised enough money through the channel to support another reef restoration project.The approach gave consumers several ways to encounter the project, since someone could see the “HOPE” reef on Google Maps, watch underwater footage, view campaign advertising or buy Sheba products. The campaign continued after its initial 2021 launch, and Sheba's current sustainability programme says that restoration efforts have expanded to multiple countries and that the Hope Grows programme now supports reef restoration at sites that go beyond Indonesia. In March 2026, Sheba also acknowledged that a regional coral disease outbreak had affected multiple reefs in the Spermonde Archipelago, including Hope Reef. The original installation was a functioning coral-restoration site that also became the centrepiece of a global advertising campaign, and the commercial result of a reported 10.4% physical-store sales lift and a 308% return on investment was unusually measurable.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2019, Oregon rebuilt 7.5 miles of Juntura Cutoff Road with recycled pavement and foamed asphalt, saving more than $2.5 million
articles.summary: Discover how Oregon's innovative use of foamed asphalt in the Juntura Cutoff Road project saved $2.5 million and expedited the construction process by nearly a month, while effectively recycling the existing road material and maintaining vital traffic flow.
articles.body: In 2019, Oregon tried a different approach to rebuilding a badly damaged rural road. Instead of removing the old pavement and starting again with new materials, the existing road was recycled in place using foamed asphalt. The method saved more than $2.5 million compared with conventional reconstruction, while also reducing the construction period by almost a month.According to the RoadResource, the project involved a 7.5-mile section of Juntura Cutoff Road, which connected the EP Minerals diatomite mine with US Highway 20. Years of heavy truck traffic had left the road with deep cracks, potholes and sections where the asphalt had completely failed. With the road serving as an important route for mine traffic, keeping it available during construction was also a major consideration.Recycling the road in placeIn the case study, the original reconstruction estimate was about $6.7 million. The alternative used cold in-place recycling with foamed asphalt, a process that allowed the existing pavement material to be reused rather than removed and hauled away. The project ultimately saved more than $2.5 million, or about 37% compared with conventional reconstruction, while recycling 100% of the existing material in place.The process involved milling about eight inches of the existing asphalt along with part of the underlying road base. The reclaimed material was then mixed with foamed asphalt, cement and water before being compacted and shaped into a new base. The Oregon Department of Transportation referred to the approach as CIREAM, a form of cold in-place recycling that uses foamed asphalt. Foamed asphalt is made by adding a small amount of water to hot asphalt binder, causing it to expand temporarily. The expanded binder can then spread through the reclaimed pavement material and bind it together. This allows the old road material to be reused in the new base without processing the entire mixture as conventional hot-mix asphalt.Keeping traffic movingThe recycling method was especially practical because Juntura Cutoff Road was the mine’s main access route, making a long closure difficult. Instead of removing the old pavement and road base and bringing in completely new material, much of the existing road was reused to form the new base. This meant less material had to be hauled away and replaced, while mine traffic could continue using the route during the work.The recycled base also became useful when the construction schedule changed. Crews had initially expected to place the 2.5-inch layer of PG 64-28 hot-mix asphalt within seven days, but the paving was delayed by about a month. In the meantime, the recycled base was left in place and kept hydrated until the final surface could be laid. The delay therefore did not mean that the newly reconstructed base had to be removed or redone. It remained part of the road while the project waited for the final paving stage.The approach was consistent with findings from wider research on foamed-asphalt cold-recycled mixtures. A study published in Construction and Building Materials found that these mixtures could provide useful engineering properties, including good water stability and high modulus, when the materials and pavement layers were properly designed. The findings help explain why foamed-asphalt recycling could work as more than simply a way to reuse old pavement: it could also provide a functional structural layer within a new road.A different way to rebuild roadsThe Juntura Cutoff Project showed that the old road could be reused as a construction material asset. The project avoided removing large amounts of old pavement and hauling in new aggregate, instead reusing material already on site. RoadResource also notes that it is possible to use the road for 20 years if maintenance activities are carried out. The road was found to have a performance comparable to that of a traditional road reconstruction project. These estimations are solely associated with the project and do not provide evidence for the longevity of all foamed roads.For the State of Oregon, the most immediate outcome was that of cost and time savings. The state now had a way to repair a badly damaged road using the existing surface material while keeping the road open and saving more than $2.5 million. This project showed that in-place recycling can help reduce road rehabilitation costs and time.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Roll-out begins for passport-free UK airport e-gates
articles.summary: The system uses facial technology to check travellers against immigration and passport information.
articles.body:
Passengers arriving into the UK will be able to pass through airport e-gates without showing their passport under a new contactless system, the government has announced.

On Tuesday, East Midlands Airport became the first airport to offer the new technology before it is rolled out to all UK airports by early 2027, the Home Office said.

The system uses facial technology so as passengers approach the e-gate, their photo is taken and then checked against immigration, travel and passport information and, if verfied, the barrier opens automatically.

Testing showed the new contactless system was up to 25% faster than using a passport, according to officials.

If further checks are needed, travellers will need to put their passport on the reader or may be directed to a Border Force officer.

Officers will continue to monitor all e-gates and offer assistance, while passengers should keep their passport with them at all times, the Home Office said.

Phil Douglas, director general of Border Force, said: "This is a win for travellers coming to our brilliant country.

"By using state-of-the-art technology, we are making journeys smoother and faster, all while fully maintaining the UK's robust border security.

"Our digital transformation also builds on our work this summer to extend eGates to children aged eight and above, making life a little easier for families."

Karen Dee, chief executive of Airports UK, the trade body for the country's airports, said the move was "excellent news for the passenger".

She added: "It is vital that we have the fast, efficient borders that arrivals into the UK now expect, and we will work closely with our members and government officials to ensure a smooth rollout."

Steve Griffiths, managing director of East Midlands Airport, in Castle Donington, Leicestershire, said: "We're delighted to be the first UK airport to have contactless e-gates introduced by Border Force.

"As an airport committed to providing an effortless travel experience, we welcome any technological innovation that can help to safely make our customers' journeys smoother, swifter and simpler.

"This complements changes that we carried out to our immigration hall recently to help improve the flow of arriving passengers through the area."

Standard e-gates are currently available at Birmingham, Bristol, Cardiff, East Midlands, Edinburgh, Gatwick, Glasgow, Heathrow, London City, Luton, Manchester, Newcastle and Stansted.

articles.title: Namibia gave rural communities wildlife rights; elephant numbers rose from about 7,500 in 1995 to 22,800 in 2016 as communal conservancies expanded
articles.summary: Discover how Namibia transformed its wildlife conservation strategy by empowering rural communities, leading to the remarkable rise of its elephant population from 7,500 to over 16,000. Learn about the successes and challenges of this community-driven approach to wildlife management.
articles.body: Namibia took an unusual approach to wildlife conservation by giving rural communities a direct stake in protecting the wildlife around them. Instead of treating wildlife only as a government resource, the country created communal conservancies where local people could manage wildlife and receive benefits from its use. The approach helped change the way communities viewed animals, particularly in areas where wildlife had once been heavily depleted.Over time, the results became clear. According to Visit Namibia, Namibia's elephant population doubled between 1995 and 2008, rising from about 7,500 animals to more than 16,000. More recent figures put the national population considerably higher, showing that the recovery continued beyond the period covered by that original comparison.Giving communities a reason to protect wildlifeThis system was introduced after Namibia became independent in 1990. Legislation was passed by the government in 1996, which allowed the formation of conservancies by communities living on communal land. Communities were entitled to conditional use of wildlife in designated zones. The first four communal conservancies were officially gazetted in 1998.These conservancies were supposed to be self-governing institutions. The residents selected committees, demarcated boundaries and created rules of resource management. This made wildlife part of the local economy through activities like photo tourism, hunting and collaboration with private tourism companies. The community would use the revenue, while conservancy game guards monitored wildlife and poaching incidents. Before the policy, people living near wildlife often received no economic benefit and still had to deal with damage to property.Wildlife began returningOne of the clearest signs of change was the return of wildlife to Namibia's communal lands, where poaching, hunting and other pressures had reduced animal populations. As conservancies expanded, local communities gained a greater role in managing wildlife outside the country's national parks. According to Visit Namibia, at least 45 per cent of Namibia's land area was under some form of conservation management by the end of 2019, including national parks, communal and commercial conservancies, private reserves and community forests.Research suggests that giving communities a greater stake in wildlife management helped make this expansion possible. A study published in Economic Affairs found that transferring certain wildlife rights to local communities had generated both economic and environmental benefits. At the same time, the researchers pointed to limitations, including incomplete rights transfers and ongoing human-wildlife conflict. This showed that community conservation was not without problems, but it had created incentives for people living alongside wildlife to protect it.The results could also be seen in individual species. Namibia's Community Conservation Programme was associated with recoveries in black rhino and other wildlife, while desert lions expanded their range in the country's northwest. Elephants showed a particularly striking increase, with one study estimating that their numbers rose from about 7,500 in 1995 to 22,800 in 2016. Together, these changes suggested that conservation was no longer confined to protected parks and reserves. Wildlife was increasingly being managed across the wider landscapes where people and animals lived alongside each other.A conservation model with challengesThe success of the conservancy system did not mean that living with wildlife became easy. More animals also meant more encounters between people and wildlife. Elephants could damage water infrastructure and crops, while predators could kill livestock. Research published in Geoforum found that increasing elephant numbers had created additional costs for some pastoral communities and raised questions about how fairly tourism revenues were distributed. This is a significant part of Namibia's conservation history. The model aimed to combine wildlife conservation with local governance and economic opportunity, but those benefits were not always shared evenly.Despite the challenges, the strategy changed how rural communities related to wildlife. Wildlife that was regarded as a natural resource of the government was integrated into local development and conservation systems. Namibia's example shows that wildlife conservation does not have to exclude local communities from access to wildlife. In some areas, involving communities in wildlife management helps encourage them to keep wildlife on the land.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Man charged with Dersingham GP Dr Hannah Terry's murder
articles.summary: A man is charged with the murder of a GP who was found dead at her home.
articles.body:
A man has been charged with the murder of a GP who was found dead at her home.

The man was arrested after the body of 45-year-old Dr Hannah Terry, also known as Hannah Cain, was found at a property in Fern Hill, Dersingham, Norfolk, on Sunday.

Norfolk Police said 45-year old Mark Cain, of Fern Hill, Dersingham, has been charged with her murder.

He has been remanded in custody until a court appearance on Wednesday.

A notice on the website of Grimston Medical Centre, where Dr Terry is listed as a member of the practice team, said it was "temporarily closed due to extremely difficult circumstances affecting our practice team".

Tributes have been left outside the centre, including a teddy bear and flowers on a bench. A card from two patients reads: "Dear Dr Hannah Terry. We are so shocked and saddened to hear such tragic news."

The Norfolk and Waveney Local Medical Committee, which represents NHS GPs, has also paid its respects.

A spokesperson said: "We are deeply saddened by the news of Dr Terry's death. She was a wonderful GP who was dedicated to providing excellent care for her patients."

Michael Devaney, from the Crown Prosecution Service, said: "The Crown Prosecution Service has decided to prosecute Mark Cain for the murder of Hannah Cain following a police investigation into an incident at her home in Dersingham.

"We have worked carefully with Norfolk Police during their investigation.

"Our thoughts remain with the family of Hannah Cain at this time."

Cain is due to appear at Norwich Magistrates' Court on Wednesday.

Dr Pallavi Devulapalli, a GP, said she was devastated when she found out her friend and former colleague had died.

She said the pair used to work together at The Hollies Surgery in Downham Market, Norfolk.

Devulapalli, who is also an independent councillor, said she "was such an easy person to work with"

"She was universally liked, she was a good GP, someone sensible who you could trust," said Devulapalli.

"I never worried about the patients she looked after - just the sort of person you want to work with," she added.

Charis-Mai Ellis, 25, paid tribute and said Terry had been her family GP.

"She had the time for you and so much empathy and understanding. You could take your time with her and she wouldn't rush," she said.

articles.title: Cornell picks former deputy US attorney general to review sex assault response
articles.summary: Sally Yates will review Cornell University's full handling of the Jane Doe sexual assault allegations involving the Chi Phi fraternity in 2024.
articles.body: Cornell University has enlisted former U.S. Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates to conduct a review of the institution's responses to sexual assault. Cornell announced the review on Tuesday, saying the review will generally cover Cornell's policies aimed at preventing and responding to sexual assault. Yates will also conduct a "detailed review of the University’s response to the allegations involving Jane Doe and members of the Chi Phi fraternity in October 2024, including whether Cornell followed its policies and procedures in responding to the matter." CORNELL CAMPUS POLICE MADE DRUG ARREST AT CHI PHI FRATERNITY HOUSE HOURS BEFORE ALLEGED GANG RAPE "The review will examine Cornell’s policies, practices and resources across the full range of prevention and response, including how reports are received and investigated; how students are supported; how hearings, disciplinary decisions and appeals are handled; the role, processes and response of campus police; coordination with other law enforcement agencies and prosecutors; campus safety reporting; and policies and oversight involving fraternities, sororities and other student organizations. It will also examine the Board’s oversight of these issues," Cornell said in a statement. Anne Meinig Smalling, who chairs the Cornell University Special Committee of Board of Trustees, said Yates will conduct a "rigorous examination" of Cornell's handling of the issue as student protests have taken over the campus this week. AOC'S DRAMATIC RETELLING OF CORNELL RAPE ALLEGATIONS COLLIDES WITH COMPLAINT DETAILS "Sally Yates brings extraordinary experience, independence and judgment to this work... The questions raised by the Jane Doe matter warrant a rigorous examination of Cornell’s response to that case, but our responsibility is broader," Smalling said in a statement. "We have asked Ms. Yates and her team to examine Cornell’s overall approach to preventing and responding to sexual misconduct, identify where we are doing things well and where we can do better, and recommend changes that will help make our community safer." Seven former Chi Phi fraternity brothers are accused in a lawsuit of drugging and raping a female Cornell student during a night of drinking, drugs and group sex at their fraternity house in October 2024. ATTORNEY FOR ACCUSED CORNELL STUDENT CALLS ON LETITIA JAMES TO STEP ASIDE OVER PRIOR COMMENTS The accuser, identified in court papers by the pseudonym Jane Doe, alleges the men sexually assaulted her after she arrived intoxicated and was pressured into taking ketamine and other substances. The men have denied wrongdoing, with some maintaining the sexual activity was consensual and others denying they participated in it. No criminal charges have been filed against the seven men. The case has now erupted into a political and legal firestorm, with New York Attorney General Letitia James announcing Friday that her office is conducting an "active criminal investigation" after Gov. Kathy Hochul appointed the Office of the Attorney General as special prosecutor. Cornell has separately agreed to retain outside counsel to conduct an independent review of the university's handling of the allegations. articles.title: Fort Cronkhite, the abandoned WWII fort near San Francisco where giant 16-inch guns once shook the city, is now a historic site surrounded by beaches, trails and Pacific Ocean views
articles.summary: Long before Fort Cronkhite became a destination for hikers, surfers and wildlife enthusiasts, it was part of a vast American military effort to prepare
articles.body: Long before Fort Cronkhite became a destination for hikers, surfers and wildlife enthusiasts, it was part of a vast American military effort to prepare for war.As World War II approached, the U.S. Army was rapidly expanding. Around 200,000 soldiers had enlisted in 1939, but by 1944, the number had surged to approximately 6 million. The sudden growth created an enormous demand for accommodation and military infrastructure, resulting in the construction of more than 100,000 temporary buildings across the country.Barracks, hospitals, offices and mess halls were built at mobilization posts, including Fort Cronkhite in California.Most of those temporary military installations disappeared after the war. Fort Cronkhite is one of the rare exceptions.Located in the Marin Headlands, overlooking the Pacific Ocean just north of San Francisco, the former military post remains one of the best-preserved examples of a WWII mobilization site and is now part of the Golden Gate National Recreation Area, according to the National Park Service (NPS).The fort that guarded San Francisco BayFort Cronkhite occupied a strategically important position. From the surrounding hills, soldiers could observe the Pacific and protect the entrance to San Francisco Bay from potential enemy attacks.The steep ridges also provided ideal locations for artillery installations.One of the most formidable was Battery Townsley, which housed two enormous 16-inch guns. The scale of the weapons reflected the seriousness of the coastal defense mission during the war.Historical records cited in the source material say that when the guns were tested in 1940, their concussion was powerful enough to break windows across San Francisco.Today, visitors can explore the restored interior of Battery Townsley and walk the trails that once formed part of the military landscape.The Cold War brought a new threatFort Cronkhite's military story did not end with World War II.During the Cold War, the nature of the perceived threat changed. Instead of preparing primarily for an attack arriving across the ocean, the U.S. military became increasingly concerned about enemy aircraft.The answer was the Nike missile system.A nearby installation at Fort Barry, known as SF-88, became part of this Cold War defense network. The site has since been preserved, offering visitors an unusual glimpse into another chapter of American military history.Together, Battery Townsley and SF-88 demonstrate how the defenses of the San Francisco Bay evolved from giant coastal guns to sophisticated missile systems.WWII barracks still surviveWhile many temporary military structures were demolished following World War II, several original buildings at Fort Cronkhite remain.One of the barracks has been restored to its original appearance, giving visitors a sense of what daily life may have been like for troops stationed in the Marin Headlands.The National Park Service has also created a self-guided History Walk, allowing visitors to explore the former base while learning about its wartime role.The beach looks unlike most California beachesThe military history is only part of the attraction.Just below Fort Cronkhite is Rodeo Beach, a distinctive stretch of coastline known for its colorful pebbles.Rather than the familiar golden sand found on many California beaches, Rodeo Beach is covered in red and green stones, including jasper, carnelian and jade.The beach is popular with surfers because of its powerful waves, although swimming is dangerous due to strong currents.Nearby Rodeo Lagoon offers a completely different landscape. The calm lagoon is surrounded by habitat that supports wildlife, but swimming is prohibited in order to protect the fragile ecosystem.Visitors can instead take the easy Rodeo Lagoon Loop, which is particularly appealing to birdwatchers.A paradise for hikers and birdwatchersThe Marin Headlands provide numerous opportunities to explore the landscape on foot or by bicycle.The Coastal Trail is one of the highlights. A short but steep section leads toward Battery Townsley, eventually opening onto dramatic views across the Pacific Ocean.The surrounding hills are particularly colorful in spring, when wildflowers attract butterflies and a variety of birds.Peregrine falcons and red-tailed hawks can be seen in the area, while migrating humpback and gray whales may occasionally be spotted offshore.The region's weather can change quickly, however. Fog and strong coastal winds are common, meaning visitors should be prepared for temperatures that can feel much colder than they might expect from the sunny conditions in San Francisco.A rare glimpse into America's Cold War pastA trip to Fort Cronkhite can also include a visit to Fort Barry and the SF-88 Nike missile site.The restored installation provides an opportunity to see how the United States prepared for a potential Cold War-era air attack.According to the supplied source material, the site is free to visit and opens on the first Saturday of every month.For history enthusiasts, the combination of Fort Cronkhite, Battery Townsley and SF-88 creates an unusual journey through several decades of American military strategy.The Marine Mammal Center is nearbyThe area also offers plenty for visitors who aren't interested in military history.Behind Fort Cronkhite is the Marine Mammal Center, a rehabilitation and research facility dedicated to helping sick and injured marine mammals.The center cares for animals including California sea lions, sea otters, harbor seals and elephant seals.Visitors can explore the facility, while additional behind-the-scenes tours provide a closer look at the rehabilitation work. Visits need to be reserved in advance.Look out for brown pelicans and whalesWildlife encounters continue along the coastline.The Bird Island overlook, beyond Rodeo Beach, is an important roosting location for brown pelicans and provides another excellent spot for birdwatching.Further along the coast stands Point Bonita Lighthouse, one of the region's most picturesque historic landmarks.Getting there involves a hike, but the scenery makes the journey worthwhile. Visitors should check opening dates before setting out because the Point Bonita Trail operates on a limited schedule.A historic destination just outside San FranciscoFort Cronkhite is roughly 10 miles north of downtown San Francisco, making it an easy addition to a Bay Area itinerary.The route takes visitors across the Golden Gate Bridge before continuing along Bunker Road toward the fort, where parking is limited.There is no camping at Fort Cronkhite itself, but several small tent-only National Park campgrounds are located in the Marin Headlands. Kirby Cove is particularly popular for its views of the Golden Gate Bridge.Today, Fort Cronkhite offers something few former military bases can: a chance to walk through surviving WWII-era structures, stand beside enormous coastal artillery, explore Cold War defenses and then hike to a Pacific beach - all within the same landscape.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1976, Kirk and Anne Douglas paid $400,000 for a Beverly Hills home and turned its garden path into a private walk of fame with more than 40 celebrity autographs; 45 years later, the estate sold for $9.015 million
articles.summary: Some homes come with history. Others have history literally written into the ground.
articles.body: Some homes come with history. Others have history literally written into the ground. In Beverly Hills, the longtime residence of Hollywood legend Kirk Douglas and his wife, Anne Douglas, offered both. Its garden path, lined with pavers bearing the signatures of more than 40 celebrated names from the entertainment world, transformed an otherwise elegant estate into a piece of living Hollywood memorabilia. Decades after the couple purchased the property, that unusual feature helped make it one of the area's most talked-about listings. The estate, known as “The Stars of Beverly Hills,” was listed for $7.495 million in December and ultimately sold for $9.015 million, attracting a buyer willing to pay a premium for its unusual connection to Hollywood's golden era, states an online report by Realtor.A Hollywood legacy underfootAccording to January 2022 report, Kirk and Anne Douglas purchased the Beverly Hills property in 1976 for $400,000. Over the years, their home became a gathering place for some of the biggest names in entertainment, with dinner parties providing the inspiration for its extraordinary garden path.Among the stars who left their signatures were Frank Sinatra, Lucille Ball, Roger Moore, Elizabeth Taylor and Jane Fonda. Members of the Douglas family also added their names, turning the pathway into a private version of the iconic Hollywood Walk of Fame, the report claims. The collection eventually grew to more than 40 celebrity autographs, giving the property an element of provenance that would be difficult, if not impossible, to recreate today, it adds.Kirk Douglas, celebrated for films including Spartacus and Paths of Glory, died in 2020 at 103. Anne Douglas died the following year at 102. Their long life together and place within Hollywood history added another layer of significance to the residence.Classic Beverly Hills livingAccording to Realtor report, beyond its famous walkway, the 1921-built home offers the proportions and character of a traditional Beverly Hills estate. The single-story residence spans 4,648 square feet and contains four bedrooms and five bathrooms. Its interiors include formal living and dining spaces alongside a family room, while the gourmet kitchen features a breakfast bar and butler's pantry. Multiple sets of glass doors open towards the grounds, creating an easy transition between the home's interior and outdoor entertaining areas.The property sits on a large, landscaped lot shaded by mature trees, offering privacy despite its central location. A resort-style swimming pool forms the centrepiece of the outdoor space, while a two-story guesthouse provides additional accommodation.A new chapterThe estate's location adds to its appeal. It sits close to the Beverly Hills Hotel, Rodeo Drive and the restaurants, shopping and amenities that have made Beverly Hills synonymous with luxury. The home is also positioned as a property that can evolve with its next owner. While its historic character remains intact, the residence offers scope for updating or expansion. Still, the most memorable part of the estate may remain the simplest: a garden path carrying the names of Hollywood royalty. For the buyer who paid $9.015 million, the property is not merely a Beverly Hills address, but a tangible piece of the city's cinematic past.Images Courtesy: People and Mansion Global You use AI every day. articles.body:
If a strange-looking message from Asos popped up on your phone today, you may be worrying what it could mean and whether you need to do anything.

The online retailer has emailed customers apologising for the "unauthorised push notification" containing an external link, adding that they should disregard the message and not click on it.

Here's what has happened, and what those who may have been affected are being advised to do.

On Tuesday morning, Asos users across the UK were sent pop-up messages from its app that appear to have been sent by hackers trying to extort the company.

"Dear ASOS DPO and IT, we have fully compromised the Snowflake instance. Engage with us, or we will leak it," the message read.

Later that day, Asos said it took immediate action to restrict the apparent hackers' access, was investigating and working with advisers and relevant authorities on "next steps".

Data storage company Snowflake told the BBC its investigations had "found no compromise" of its platform.

At this stage it isn't clear what information, if any, has been accessed.

On Tuesday evening, Asos told customers it may include "basic personal information including name and contact details".

"However, we don't believe that any payment-card information or account passwords have been impacted," it added.

While those who received the pop-up message will undoubtedly be concerned, it does not mean your phone has been hacked.

Don't click the link: The hack notification included a link to a Telegram account - Asos and cyber security experts say not to click on it

Change passwords: It's worth updating your password, including across other sites that use the same one as your Asos account. The advice for a strong password is to mix numbers, symbols and upper and lower case characters, and avoid using the same password across multiple accounts

Turn on two-step verification for important apps like banking and email: The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) calls this "one of the most effective ways to protect your online accounts from cyber criminals". You can usually turn it on by going into the security settings in your account

Monitor transactions: Keep an eye on your online transactions for anything unusual

According to Charlotte Wilson, head of enterprise at global cyber-security firm Check Point, "the biggest immediate risk may be what happens next".

She says criminals know people will be searching for information online and expects there to be "attempts to exploit that confusion".

Her advice to Asos customers is not to be "scared and frightened". But she says they should be "extremely suspicious" of emails, texts or messages claiming their account has been compromised, offering a refund or asking them to click a link to reset their password.

People should hang up the phone if they receive any calls from someone they think might be posing as Asos or another organisation, says Which? spokesperson Kat Cereda.

The consumer rights expert says they should contact the organisation themselves afterwards through separate means.

It's been less than 24 hours since the notification popped up on people's phones, and there are a number of unanswered questions.

It isn't yet clear who is behind the message, what their motivation is, how many people received the notification or how many may be impacted

Wilson, from the cyber-security firm Check Point, says there's still "an awful lot" we don't know.

Asos said its website and app were operating "as normal, and customers can continue to shop with confidence on ASOS as normal" as of Tuesday night.

It said protecting customers "is our priority", and it will provide a further update "as soon as we have confirmed more information".

People should visit Asos's official website directly for updates.

articles.title: Jammu and Kashmir: Arms & drugs seized in cross-border smuggling case; 4 held
articles.summary: JAMMU: J&K Police have arrested four suspects, including one from Punjab, in connection with the alleged cross-border smuggling of drugs and arms via
articles.body: JAMMU: J&K Police have arrested four suspects, including one from Punjab, in connection with the alleged cross-border smuggling of drugs and arms via drones in the border village of Arnia in Jammu district. An Italy-made Beretta pistol, two magazines, four live rounds, and over 1kg of narcotics were seized during subsequent searches, police said Tuesday.On Oct 3, cops manning a checkpoint at Arnia’s Tamala Bridge stopped two men moving on a bike around 10.45pm. One of the men, Rahul Kumar, was found carrying 264g of suspected heroin, a Beretta pistol, two magazines and four live rounds. Another 276g of suspected heroin was seized from the second man, Ajay Kumar Talhar. Both are residents of Arnia.During questioning, the accused allegedly confessed their links with Pakistan-based handlers and admitted to having received two air-dropped consignments in the past. Information obtained from the duo led cops to a third suspect, also named Ajay Kumar. He was arrested with 464g of opium resin and 13.3g of heroin, police said.Further probe revealed the involvement of a fourth suspect—Jaganpreet Randhawa alias Jaggi, believed to be a forward link in the smuggling nexus—who was arrested in Punjab.Arnia PS registered an FIR under relevant sections of the NDPS and Arms Acts. Officials said further investigation was underway.Many such cases have earlier been reported from forward areas along the Indo-Pak international border and the Line of Control in J&K. articles.title: Trump, Waltz link France riots to mass immigration as thousands are arrested
articles.summary: Trump claims France's student protests are about "Islam wanting to take over" as Sébastien Lecornu reports the school system's heaviest toll in decades.
articles.body: FIRST ON FOX: President Donald Trump warned Tuesday that France’s escalating riots were being driven by "out of control mass migration," as U.S. Ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz echoed those concerns and blamed unchecked immigration and broader European policy failures for helping fuel the unrest. Asked by Fox News Digital about Trump’s comments and the scenes emerging from France, Waltz condemned the violence while also linking the unrest to European immigration and economic policies. "I think we would always condemn lawlessness, condemn the violence that we're seeing in Paris," Waltz told Fox News Digital. "But I think we also have to recognize that when you have open borders, when you [have] this pro-migration, unchecked immigration kind of policy, coupled with policies over the years that deny people basic energy, that overspend on all kinds of other government programs, that you see a level of frustration boiling to the surface." FRANCE EXPLODES AGAIN AS STUDENTS RIOT OVER EDUCATION Trump weighed in as the unrest intensified, arguing that what was unfolding went beyond the students’ complaints about France’s education system. "What’s happening in France is nothing less than out of control mass migration. This isn’t about schools, this is about Islam wanting to take over a once great Country!" Trump wrote on Truth Social Tuesday. "Unfortunately, I think you're seeing the results of some of that, and President Trump has brought that to light," Waltz added. The comments came as France faced its biggest day of school unrest since the protests began in September. On Tuesday, police fired tear gas in Paris and other major cities, protesters lit fires and hurled projectiles, and France’s Interior Ministry said 6,100 people had been arrested, the overwhelming majority of them minors, according to Reuters. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu described the clashes as producing the school system’s "heaviest toll in decades". FRANCE’S VIOLENT STUDENT PROTESTS RAISE WARNING FOR AMERICA: ‘A CAUTIONARY TALE’ France’s Interior Ministry said 6,100 people have been arrested so far, the overwhelming majority of them minors. Lecornu told lawmakers Tuesday that at least 215 teenagers and 85 school staff members have been injured, while his office said more than 700 police officers have also been hurt, according to Reuters. The latest demonstrations brought clashes in Paris, Lyon, Strasbourg and Rennes, where police fired tear gas as protesters lit fires and hurled projectiles. More than half of France’s roughly 3,700 high schools were blockaded or expected to close Tuesday, according to the High School Students Union. The ⁠Paris police said the clashes there had come about when some 300 people attempted to face off against security forces, adding that the protest was generally unfolding well elsewhere. Theo Wold, a former assistant attorney general and former White House deputy assistant for domestic policy under Trump, also argued that immigration was contributing to the unrest. FRANCE ROCKED BY STUDENT RIOTS AS HUNDREDS ARRESTED, VIOLENCE SPREADS NATIONWIDE "The French are notorious for strikes, labor stoppages and street demonstrations. It’s a core part of the Fifth Republic’s civic culture," Wold told Fox News Digital. "What’s new is the violence, lawlessness and rioting. This is a consequence of mass immigration." While Trump, Waltz and Wold linked the violence to immigration, Reuters and AP have reported that the protest movement began over school conditions, including teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms, deteriorating buildings and education funding. Students have cited overcrowded classrooms, teacher shortages and deteriorating school buildings — including water leaks and rat infestations — among their grievances. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The unrest has increasingly become part of a broader political fight ahead of France’s presidential election in April and May 2027. Reuters reported last week that French authorities and political opponents have accused lawmakers and mayors from the hard-left France Unbowed party, or LFI, of stoking the demonstrations. LFI has denied the accusations. Fox News Digital's Greg Norman-Diamond and Reuters contributed to this story.

articles.title: Democrats debate Kamala Harris 2028 run as surrogate says party wants to 'move on' from 2024 loss
articles.summary: Kamala Harris allies questioned whether her respect within the Democratic Party translates to real support for a 2028 presidential election bid.
articles.body: Allies of former Vice President Kamala Harris, as well as Democratic surrogates, are questioning whether the former Democratic nominee would be the top choice within the party, weighing her name recognition and respect among Democrats against the notion that voters want to move on. "People just want to move on," Fletcher Smith, a former state legislator in South Carolina and Biden 2020 surrogate, told The Washington Post. "We’ve got a number of younger generation of people who are capable of leading — we’ve got governors, we’ve got congresspeople, we have senators. I think what she needs to do is sit out 2028 and let some other people have a shot at saving our democracy." Many Democratic allies noted Harris is well respected within the party, but questioned whether respect translated into support. DEMOCRATS SHY AWAY FROM QUESTIONS ON WHETHER HARRIS SHOULD RUN FOR PRESIDENT IN 2028 "She’s extraordinarily popular in the party and people are very fond of her and want her to be treated with a lot of respect and deference — given all the due of someone in her position," Jamal Simmons, a former communications director for Harris, told the Post. "Many people see it as a service what she did in 2024, where she really stepped up for the party, stepped up for Joe Biden, stepped up for the country. There’s a lot of respect for her. But it’s yet to be seen how much of that becomes support for another presidential run." Podcast host and former South Carolina state senator Bakari Sellers told the Post that though she is" very talented," she has yet to define what a potential 2028 run would look like to key constituencies. "One of the first statements she put out was about AI, when it’s clear she needs to boost her support among Black men," Sellers told the Post. "California has a cost-of-living issue, and she’s not talking about cost of living at all." The Post reported that Sellers said he hasn't spoken to Harris in over a year. He suggested that was concerning for a candidate who would need a victory in South Carolina, according to the report. HARRIS STOPS IN KEY PRESIDENTIAL PRIMARY STATE AFTER LEAVING DOOR WIDE OPEN TO 2028 RUN During Sellers' podcast on Monday, he listed Harris as No. 2 in his top five candidates for 2028. He said Harris was talented and intelligent, but questioned whether her team would "let her be great." "Let Kamala be Kamala, and you would have the next president of the United States without a doubt in my mind," he said. The podcast host ranked Maryland Gov. Wes Moore in the No. 1 spot, calling him the "biggest impediment" to Harris being the nominee. WATCH: DEM SENATORS DODGE BACKING KAMALA HARRIS IN POTENTIAL 2028 RUN: ‘VERY MESSY’ Democratic strategist Kaivan Shroff, who was part of Hillary Clinton's 2016 campaign, told Fox News Digital that Harris hasn't done anything differently since 2024. "Harris has not done anything truly new or different since 2024. Her greatest post-VP visibility came from her book tour. Running again without a new chapter or story to tell is like reapplying to the same college after getting rejected, taking a gap year, and coming back with basically the same application. You can rewrite the essay, but if you did nothing new, admissions is still looking at the same file," Shroff said. Shroff suggested somebody new might have the advantage over her because they would be introducing themselves to voters for the first time on a national stage. "She does not get to reintroduce herself. That is the burden of being so well known. She has a real base and a lot of goodwill in the party, but she also lost, and that makes some voters and, importantly, donors nervous. Even if she starts high in the polls, the question is where the growth comes from if there is not much new to add," he said. "Someone like a Pritzker at least gets the advantage of telling his story to a lot of voters for the first time." Shroff added, "What Harris is doing well right now is using her position as a party leader rather than acting like a candidate in waiting. A great example is her showing up for Abdul El-Sayed despite his criticism of her and the bad blood with some on the far left in Michigan. She acknowledged the disagreements, still made the case for him, and used her stature to help unite the party in a critical moment — particularly with outreach to Black voters. That is an example of influence she has right now, regardless of what she does in 2028 and that will continue to matter whether she seeks the nomination or not." California Gov. Gavin Newsom said during a recent interview that he would not run in 2028 if Harris planned to run. DEM MEGADONOR UNLEASHES REALITY CHECK ON HARRIS FOR 2028 WHILE EYEING SOCIALIST FIREBRAND Harris has not been definitive on whether she plans to run, but has said she is thinking about it. Others were more confident in Harris, including Ashley Etienne, another former communications director for the former VP. She told the Post that Harris would need to separate herself from the Democratic establishment, but said she would have major advantages in a national election. CARVILLE DOESN'T 'FEEL SORRY' FOR URGING DEMOCRATS TO MOVE ON FROM THE KAMALA HARRIS ERA "It’s almost like, why not her? She has proven, unlike anyone else in the race, that she’s got these advantages that will matter in a national election," she told the Post. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Virginia Democratic state senator L. Louise Lucas told the Post that Democrats rejecting Harris too fast could be interpreted as a negative political move as well, suggesting it could be seen as overlooking a qualified Black woman for the position. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "There’s no question that people would be upset because you see what happened last time," Lucas told the Post. "It could very well be that some folks would be so disillusioned that they would just say, ‘I give up on this process’ — especially people who’ve been fighting as many years as I have, who have come through the civil rights movement and just experienced so much, endured so much, and then to see this happen again would be quite painful." Several members of Congress didn't rush to throw their support behind Harris when asked by Fox News Digital about her possibly running in 2028. "Well, I've backed her before, but there'll be other contenders this time," Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., told Fox News Digital. "I've made no decisions about who I would support." "I think we're going to have a very, very, very messy and very big primary," Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., said. "It's going to be every Tom, Dick and Harry. And that's probably where it should be." "We're focused on 2026," said Sen. Angela Alsobrooks, D-Md. "We're going to win back the House and the Senate." She continued, "I love Kamala Harris. I have a very personal friendship and relationship. She's amazing. I think anybody who wants to run should. She's obviously very well qualified. We need to focus on '26."

articles.title: Ex-US spy found with $40m in gold bars pleads guilty to wire fraud
articles.summary: David Rush, who also confessed to providing secrets to a foreign government, had revealed the existence of a "clandestine human source", prosecutors said.
articles.body:
A former CIA official arrested in May, who had more than $40m (£30.1m) in gold bars taken from work in his home, has pleaded guilty to wire fraud.

A federal judge on Tuesday approved a plea deal between David Rush, 49, and federal prosecutors requiring him to pay nearly $200m in restitution to the government and forfeit luxury real estate, cars, watches and other assets tied to his crime.

As part of the deal, Rush also confessed to providing secrets to a foreign government, which could have caused "grave damage" to national security.

"The defendant will plead guilty because the defendant is in fact guilty of the charged offense," prosecutors stated in a court filing outlining the deal.

The BBC has contacted Rush's lawyer, who declined to comment.

Rush was initially charged with theft of public funds. At the time of his arrest, a raid on his home uncovered 298 gold bars that he had received for "work-related expenses".

A federal judge will set his sentence at a later date, and a hearing has been scheduled for 28 January. The charge carries a maximum prison sentence of 20 years, but prosecutors noted that the time can be added to under federal law.

Court filings around the deal bring new details to light, including that Rush revealed the existence and description of a "clandestine human source" to a foreign official.

"The disclosure of such information could endanger the safety and life of the human source and the US government officers working with the source and jeopardize the US government's ability to recruit human sources, who rely on the US government's assurances of absolute secrecy," prosecutors said in the filing.

In a news release, CIA Director John Ratcliffe said Rush "abused his position and betrayed the public trust and should be held fully accountable for his actions".

FBI investigators said that between November 2025 to March 2026 Rush made repeated requests for "a significant quantity of foreign currency and tens of millions of dollars in gold bars for work-related expenses".

"Rush fabricated a highly classified program to justify the acquisition of luxury real estate in South Florida, which he then intended to resell for personal profit," the court filing laying out the deal states.

Rush "effectively acted as his own approving official, enabling him to expend substantial amounts of United States government money without meaningful scrutiny", according to the filing.

He then used "fraudulently obtained" public funds to acquire luxury real estate properties in southern Florida.

The wire transfer charge was related to a $45m transfer that he initiated in January 2026. The plea deal also says that he provided top secret data to "a foreign government official who was not authorised to receive it and had no need to know it".

Along with the gold bars, Rush was also found with $2m in cash and 35 luxury watches.

Prosecutors said Rush was moving funds into commodities that could be easily traded, citing "strong evidence" he was trying to hide the money.

Under the deal, he is also required to turn in the watches and two BMW vehicles, along with the cash and nearly $39m that was seized from his bank account.

In June, US Magistrate Judge William Fitzpatrick cited Rush's professional career in deciding he was a flight risk, and ordered him held in jail pending trial.

"He's in a different position than most people to flee and avoid detection by law enforcement," he said.

Court records do not go into detail about Rush's work for the CIA, and describe him as a former senior executive in a US government agency in Virginia who had top secret clearance and access to classified information.

US media have confirmed his former employment with the CIA. According to The Washington Post , he was senior executive in the agency's Directorate of Science and Technology, which develops high-tech spy tools.

He had also previously been accused of fraudulently taking military leave with pay after being honourably discharged from the US Navy, and for lying about his education and military service when applying for his job in 2009. Court records show Rush was accused of falsely telling employers he had been a navy pilot.

"These and other representations concerning Rush's military and academic accomplishments were false," the plea deal filing states.

The government had argued previously that large sums of the funds are still unaccounted for, a claim which his lawyer has denied.

articles.title: Antique miniature paintings of Banaras on display
articles.summary: Banaras Gharana miniature paintings exhibition opens at Kokoro Art Gallery, Lucknow; 39 natural pigment works span five generations, open Oct 7–28.
articles.body: Lucknow: The centuries-old miniature painting tradition of the Banaras Gharana was on display at Kokoro Art gallery on Tuesday with the inauguration of ‘MINIATURES: Banaras Gharana’.Curated by Vandana Sehgal, the exhibition was inaugurated by Amrit Abhijat (IAS), additional chief secretary, department of tourism, culture and transport. The exhibition will remain open to visitors from Oct 7 to 28, between 11 am and 7 pm.Titled ‘A Repertoire of Paintings by Generations’, the exhibition brings together 39 works created with natural pigments and traces the artistic lineage across five generations of the Banaras miniature tradition. The works on display represent artists including Ustad Mulchand Prasad, Ustad Ram Prasad, Ustad Sharda Prasad, Ustad Mukund Prasad, Ustad Gopal Prasad and Vansh Shri Yadav. Ankit Prasad said, “The exhibition highlights how the guru-shishya tradition has preserved the technical discipline of Mughal miniature painting while allowing it to evolve through Banaras’ religious, cultural and social landscape.”Fine drawing, delicate brushwork, natural pigments, controlled colour composition and intricate detailing are among the defining features of the tradition. Seventh-generation artist and son of Mukund Prasad, artist Ankit Prasad said, “I have learnt the art of painting and use of colours from my ancestors. I feel truly happy and proud to carry forward my family’s rich artistic legacy and keep its traditions alive.”The Banaras school developed through a lineage linked to Mughal court painting and gradually absorbed local themes, including deities, nature, social life and Indian cultural symbols. Artists such as Mulchand Prasad and Ram Prasad played a significant role in carrying the tradition across painting, murals, illustration and portraiture.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.body: NEW DELHI: The opposition's protest march to Election Commission headquarters on the SIR-CEC issue Tuesday turned into a high-octane confrontation between Modi govt and INDIA bloc, leading to an eight-hour dharna by Rahul Gandhi and his colleagues at Akashvani Bhavan and ending with their detention in late-evening police action.Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other Congress MPs and functionaries forced their way onto the Akashvani premises, after the march by a large contingent of INDIA bloc-BJD MPs was stopped midway by police. The MPs, including Mallikarjun Kharge, Akhilesh Yadav, Sanjay Raut, Supriya Sule and Abhishek Banerjee, started from Parliament for the EC office amid slogans targeting PM Narendra Modi, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and BJP. But the group was stopped just metres away by heavy police deployment and barricades.The marchers, aided by Congress and SP workers, sat on a dharna on the road outside Akashvani Bhavan. Rahul climbed on top of a police barricade, waving the Tricolour. After an hour, they were detained and taken away in buses.But as they were being led away, Rahul, Priyanka, MPs KC Venugopal, Deepender Hooda, Charanjit Channi, Praniti Shinde, Raja Warring, Pawan Khera and others pushed their way into the Akashvani lawns and sat under a tree. Pleas by cops to vacate the premises went unheeded, prolonging the controversy BJP perh-aps believed would end with the whisking away of MPs.Congress sources claimed govt approached through police and offered permission for five-seven members to meet the CEC, but the party brass insisted on a larger contingent comprising all alliance partners. Rahul is also said to have sought an alternative place for the dharna, like Rajghat.With govt unwilling, cops swooped down on the protesters. They were said to have been taken to Kingsway camp.Those present at the march included Rajeev Shukla, Kumari Selja, Sandosh Kumar, Kalyan Banerjee, Mahua Moitra, Manickam Tagore, Jairam Ramesh, Iqra Hasan, Harendra Malik, Karamvir Boudh, Manas Mangaraj, Rajaram Singh, Sudama Singh, Sasmit Patra, Dharmendra Yadav and Derek O'Brien.Rahul said Modi, home minister Amit Shah and RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat had hijacked the country, and would face action for "treason".Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Wisconsin homeowner vows to fight proposed data-center power line after utility offered $81,000 plus $50,000 to clear a 1,000-by-75-foot corridor and remove six outbuildings
articles.summary: For more than three decades, Jerry Zelenka and his wife have built their Wisconsin property piece by piece, turning raw land into a home surrounded by
articles.body: For more than three decades, Jerry Zelenka and his wife have built their Wisconsin property piece by piece, turning raw land into a home surrounded by trees, barns and working outbuildings. Now, a proposed transmission line tied to a planned data center in nearby Port Washington could dramatically alter the property, leaving the 75-year-old homeowner facing the prospect of losing much of what he spent years creating. The Fredonia homeowner says American Transmission Co. has proposed a new route across his property, including a cleared corridor, the removal of six structures and a 130-foot transmission tower near his driveway. He intends to challenge the plan rather than voluntarily accept the terms, states an online report by Washington County Insider.A new Route, a bigger disputeThe current proposal follows an earlier application that the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin rejected as incomplete, according to Zelenka. ATC subsequently submitted a new application featuring revised plans and routes.Under the latest proposal, Zelenka's property would sit along the route now being considered. The planned transmission corridor would stretch roughly 1,000 feet by 75 feet across his land, requiring substantial clearing of trees and vegetation. The affected area includes a shed, chicken coop, hog barn, barn, garage and machine shed. Mature cedars, oaks, ash, elm and black walnut trees would also be removed as part of the proposed clearing.The cost of giving up the landAccording to Zelenka, ATC has offered $81,000 to compensate for the buildings and property impacts. An additional one-time payment of $50,000 is being offered if he signs an agreement at this stage.For Zelenka, the proposed compensation does not come close to replacing what would be lost. He questions how the property could retain its current value with a large transmission tower and high-voltage infrastructure positioned close to the house, states the online report.The proposal would leave the home standing while stripping away much of the surrounding infrastructure that has defined the property for decades. At his age, Zelenka says rebuilding the structures or relocating is not a realistic option.A property built over decadesThe dispute carries particular weight because of the history behind the property. Zelenka and his wife purchased the land on Highway A in the winter of 1990. They cleared the site, sourced timber and built their home themselves, initially living in a shed while construction continued. Over the years, the couple planted hundreds of trees through a state Department of Natural Resources programme and added buildings to the property. Some of the timber used in the barn came from century-old cedar logs Zelenka obtained locally. The landscape is therefore more than a collection of structures and trees. It represents decades of work and investment.Eminent domain at the centreAccording to the online report, the dispute could ultimately extend beyond negotiations. Zelenka is concerned that ATC could pursue eminent domain if property owners refuse to accept the proposed terms.Two neighbouring property owners, who are attorneys, are already challenging the issue in federal court. At the heart of the legal dispute is whether land can be taken for a transmission project primarily intended to serve a private data-center development.For Zelenka, that question is central to the fight. He maintains that the proposed project would fundamentally change his property for infrastructure connected to a private business.As the transmission project moves through the regulatory process, the Wisconsin homeowner remains opposed to surrendering the land voluntarily. What began as a family effort to build a home and cultivate a piece of countryside has become a much larger battle over property rights, infrastructure and the rapidly expanding power demands of data centers.Images Courtesy: Washington County InsiderYou use AI every day. articles.title: Paul Allen turned a 250-foot research vessel into a deep-sea wreck hunter; it found USS Indianapolis 5,500 metres below the Pacific
articles.summary: Paul Allen's research vessel Petrel was built to monitor Norwegian offshore oil and gas infrastructure, but it went on to find some of the best-known
articles.body: Paul Allen's research vessel Petrel was built to monitor Norwegian offshore oil and gas infrastructure, but it went on to find some of the best-known ships lost in the Second World War. According to a Navy News Service report, Petrel's expedition crew located the wreck of USS Indianapolis, a ship sunk on 30 July 1945, in water more than 18,000 feet deep. The cruiser went down in 12 minutes, and only 316 or 317 of the 1,196 crewmen aboard survived, depending on which figure in the report is used. The Navy bought Petrel in 2022 and now operates it as Sarah Lynn.Why did USS Indianapolis sink 5,500 metres below the PacificAccording to the US Department of War, the ship was torpedoed by a Japanese submarine in the early morning hours of 30 July 1945 and sank in 12 minutes. This made it impossible to send a distress signal or deploy much of its life-saving equipment. Before the attack, the report adds, Indianapolis had completed a secret mission delivering components of the atomic bomb used at Hiroshima. A photograph caption in the same report identifies the vessel as a Portland-class heavy cruiser. It says the ship was sunk in the Philippine Sea after delivering parts for the first atomic bomb used in combat to the US air base at Tinian.1,196 crewmen were aboard, and about 300 went down with the ship. The rest faced exposure, dehydration, saltwater poisoning and shark attacks while floating with few lifeboats and almost no food or water. The Navy learned of the sinking only when survivors were spotted four days later by the crew of a PV-1 Ventura on routine patrol. The report gives two survivor figures: the caption says only 317 survived, while the main text says only 316 survived after four to five days in the water.How did Paul Allen turn Petrel into a deep-sea wreck hunterPetrel is a 250-foot vessel that Allen had recently acquired and retrofitted with state-of-the-art subsea equipment capable of diving three and a half miles. Robert Kraft, Allen's director of subsea operations, is quoted as saying that the team had assembled and integrated this technology, assets and capability into an operating platform. He described it as one of the very few on the planet. He adds that Petrel was originally built to monitor Norwegian offshore oil and gas infrastructure before Allen bought the ship in 2016. It states that Allen and his company Vulcan then outfitted the ship with millions of dollars of sensors and remotely operated vehicles for its new role as an underwater archaeology platform.Another key factor in the discovery was research carried out in 2016 by Dr Richard Hulver, a historian with the Naval History and Heritage Command. His work identified a naval landing craft that had recorded a sighting of Indianapolis hours before it was torpedoed. This led to a new search area west of the original presumed position. Using that information, the research team developed a new position and estimated search area, which still covered 600 square miles of open ocean. The report also lists other discoveries by Allen-led expeditions: the Japanese battleship Musashi in March 2015 and the Italian destroyer Artigliere in March 2017. His team also retrieved and restored the ship's bell from HMS Hood for presentation to the British Navy.How did the Petrel expedition survey the USS Indianapolis wreckA 13-person expedition team on Petrel was surveying the full site and was due to conduct a live tour of the wreckage within a few weeks. Officials said the team's work complied with US law, treated the sunken ship as a war grave and did not disturb the site. Indianapolis remains the property of the US Navy, and its location will remain confidential and restricted by the Navy. It adds that the Petrel crew had collaborated with Navy authorities throughout the search and would continue to work on plans to honour the 22 crew members still alive at the time, as well as the families of all those who served on the cruiser.The Navy bought Petrel in 2022 for $12.5 million after the estate of Microsoft co-founder Allen liquidated some of his assets. It states that the ship capsized in a drydock in Scotland in 2023, causing unspecified damage. Officials confirmed that the ship, now named MV Sarah Lynn, is the former Petrel, and lists among the wrecks it found USS Juneau, the Japanese carrier Kaga and the carriers Lexington, Wasp and Hornet. Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command told USNI News that the ship was rechristened in 2025 and is operated by Oceaneering International on behalf of the Navy. Its statement describes Sarah Lynn as a "multi-purpose maritime operations vessel".You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
